messages.subject: Mediation with latent variable
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone,

Does blavaan support analysis of mediations that include latent variables in this version?

Thank you,

lf

messages.subject: Re: Mediation with latent variable
messages.body_plain:
Luis,

It might help to see your specific model, but blavaan should allow you to do a mediation analysis similar to below (using latent variables instead of observed):

http://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/mediation.html

Ed

messages.subject_clean: Error in object1@test[[1]] : subscript out of bounds
messages.body_plain:
If you haven't, you might also check that you have the newest version of lavaan (separately from blavaan).

But, in your case, I think the test="none" argument is the culprit. blavCompare() will not work with this argument (and I should add a check for this).

You might also consider using the scale() function on more observed variables, because I also see a warning about observed variances being very different from each another.

Ed

messages.subject: Re: Error in object1@test[[1]] : subscript out of bounds
messages.subject_clean: Error in object1@test[[1]] : subscript out of bounds
messages.body_plain:
Davide,

As we discussed off-list, the error appears to go away when incomplete cases are removed. In the "incomplete data" case, I believe the issue is related to this:

https://groups.google.com/forum/#!msg/lavaan/00SVZOOwclk/Fixgg03WPmwJ;context-place=forum/lavaan

Looking at your model some more, there might also be problems stemming from the latent variable "Intercept" because there is only one observed variable corresponding to it. Instead, the observed variable "int" could have a regression relationship with other lvs. You might try something like this

model_Learn_cfa_free <- '
# latent variables
OS =~ score_OS + score_SS
PET =~ math + hebrew
Gf =~ ETS_V + ETS_Loc
CRT_arb=~ crt_112 + crt_212
CRT_narb=~ crt_111 + crt_211
int ~ OS + PET + Gf + CRT_arb + CRT_narb
'

fitLearn_bcfa_free <- bcfa(model_Learn_cfa_free, data=mc)

And then the constrained model could just have int ~ 1 instead of the last line.

Ed

messages.subject: Reporting fit indices and convergence
messages.body_plain:
First of all, I want to thank blavaan's authors. The package is great!

I need some recommendations about reporting blavaan analysis:
1. To claim for good fitting of a model to the data, is it sufficient to report ppp? Are there other fit indices that are usually reported?
2. To claim for convergence of the model, is it sufficient to report PSRF of parameter estimations? Is there any other useful information about this topic, worth to report?
3. I have read some papers that present two types of plots: trace plots and Gelman-Rubin convergence statistic R. Is it possible to obtain this previous  plot type (Gelman-Rubin) with blavaan?

Hi all

I am here to announce a Summer course that may be of interest. I am teaching a Bayesian SEM course as part of the Stats Camp in Albuquerque New Mexico this June 12-16.
The example and code for class are provided with blavaan and JAGS (if interested in using other software we can provide support). For more information please visit the website below, and feel free to ask me questions

Thanks

messages.body_plain:
Celia,

For your #1 and #2, the statistics you mention are probably most popular. There is a little discussion and further references in the blavaan paper:

https://arxiv.org/abs/1511.05604

For #3, there is not currently built-in functionality to plot Gelman-Rubin statistics (to clarify, this is the same as PSRF in your point 2). But you can extract them (then plot them yourself) via

blavInspect(fit, 'psrf')

Ed
